Age Calculator

브라우저 내부 처리

Get an exact age from a birth date, plus date differences, D-day countdowns and date arithmetic on one screen.

Negative values move backwards. Business days skip weekends only, not public holidays.

Working with ages and date spans

Korea switched to international age for laws and contracts in June 2023, so documents often mix three different age counts. This page resolves all three and handles the surrounding date math.

Three age counts

Exact age increases on the birthday. Korean counting age increases when the calendar year changes. Year age is simply the current year minus the birth year, used in conscription and youth protection law. The same person can differ by up to two years across the three.

Inclusive or exclusive days

Hotel nights, working days and event spans usually count the first day too, so both the plain difference and the inclusive count are shown. Check which one the contract wording means.

Everything stays local

Birth dates and target dates are calculated in the current browser and never sent to a server or stored. Nothing remains once the tab is closed.

Things to check

Month math clamps to the last day

Adding one month to January 31 gives February 28, not March 3. The same clamping rule is used for the month portion of a date difference so the two features agree.

Business days skip weekends only

Only Saturday and Sunday are excluded. Public holidays change every year and are not applied, so the result can differ from an actual working calendar.

Time zone

Today's date follows the device time zone. Away from Korea it can be a day off, so set the reference date explicitly when that matters.

More: step-by-step usage and worked examples

How to use it

  1. Enter a birth date on the Age tab to see exact, Korean counting and year ages side by side.
  2. Change the reference date to view an age at a past or future point. Leave it blank to use today.
  3. On the Date difference tab, enter two dates to get days, inclusive days and weekdays excluding weekends.
  4. The D-day tab counts toward a target date; the Add tab shifts a base date by years, months, weeks, days or business days.
